subject: Why are you running only Z1 and Z2 on your paper? but suggested from Z1 to Z5

messages.author: 52e8852d3d095824
messages.subject: Why are you running only Z1 and Z2 on your paper? but suggested from Z1 to Z5
parts:
Hello Author,

Please see the attached. I ran Titan for 5 tumor populations (Z1-Z5). Correct me if I am wrong. The cellular prevalence figure showed presence of 5 tumor subclones although most are in Z4 and Z5.

The parameter results are:

Normal contamination estimate: 0.23
Average tumour ploidy estimate: 2.03
Clonal cluster cellular prevalence Z=5: 1.0000 0.9361 0.8376 0.5582 0.2758
Number of iterations: 7
Log likelihood: -5267033.7196
S_Dbw dens.bw (LogRatio): 0.0097 
S_Dbw scat (LogRatio): 0.0250 
S_Dbw validity index (LogRatio): 0.0348 
S_Dbw dens.bw (AllelicRatio): 0.1202 
S_Dbw scat (AllelicRatio): 0.0146 
S_Dbw validity index (AllelicRatio): 0.1348 
S_Dbw dens.bw (Both): 0.1299 
S_Dbw scat (Both): 0.0396 
S_Dbw validity index (Both): 0.1695 

So, I think Z5 was chosen to be optimal in this case. Am I right?

Can I rerun and set numClusters=2 (the same as your paper) based on the present result? I like to reduce the noise generated in the cellular prevalence figure due to small number of CNA observed in Z1, Z2 and Z3.

Thank you for you suggestion. I look forward to hearing from you.

Cheers,
James

messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: Why are you running only Z1 and Z2 on your paper? but suggested from Z1 to Z5
parts:
Hi James,

Typically, TITAN is run 5 times - once for each setting of numClusters equal to 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5.  You have run only numClusters=5.  You should now run it for 1, 2, 3, and 4 as well.  You can then compare the S_Dbw validity index to find the one solution (out of the 5 runs) that has the minimum value.

From the plot that you have attached, it appears the allele ratio data (middle panel) is quite noisy and is leading to an over-segmented result.  Please consider only keeping SNPs that are also present in HapMap or 1000G.  

Hope this helps.

Best,
Gavin
